PullRequest.Title: agentHost: report calls to tools the session does not offer as unknown
PullRequest.Body:
When the model calls a tool name the session does not offer, the Copilot runtime fails the call with the generic `failure` code. `agentHost.toolInvoked` and the Agent Host's `languageModelToolInvoked` therefore counted it as a built-in (`agentHost`) tool that failed, which can't be told apart from a real tool that ran and failed. Over a week this added thousands of invented names such as `view_range`, `str_replace` and `powerShell` to the built-in tool set.

Addresses part 2 of microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10891.

### Changes

- A call to a tool the session does not offer now reports `toolSourceKind: unknown` and `errorCode: toolNotFound`.
- Its `toolId` is a `sha256:` hash of the requested name, because the name is arbitrary model output.
- The runtime sends no dedicated error code, so the host recognizes these calls by the runtime's error message, `Tool '<name>' does not exist.`. The runtime uses the same check itself (`resume_result_reports_missing_tool`). If that wording changes, these calls are reported as built-in failures again, as they are today.
- The GDPR comments for `toolId`, `toolSourceKind` and `errorCode` on `agentHost.toolInvoked`, and `AGENTS.md`, describe the new values.

Not changed: MCP tools without a VS Code customization still report `agentHost`, and the raw names of other tools are tracked in microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10914.

### How to test

- `npm run test-node -- --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostToolCallTelemetry.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostToolCallTracker.test.ts`: 25 passing. The new test uses the runtime's actual error payload (`{ message: "Tool 'view_range' does not exist.", code: "failure" }`, taken from a real session log) and fails without the change. A built-in tool that fails with another "does not exist" message keeps `agentHost`/`failure`.
- `npm run test-node -- --runGlob "vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/*.test.js"`: 14,204 passing, 77 pending.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passes.
- Not run: a manual check in an Agents window session where the model calls a tool that doesn't exist.

Scenarios.Scenario: Complete a real built-in, MCP, or client tool call, including ordinary failures, in a main or subagent chat.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: AgentSideEffects dispatches the completion to session state before synchronously invoking toolCallCompleted. Result-size serialization and report preparation run on the host event loop; collector delivery is not awaited. The new predicate short-circuits successful calls and non-agentHost contributors; ordinary built-in failures only compare the error-message prefix.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per completed call with a matching timing entry, proportional to serialized result bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical JSON.stringify(result).length was already executed once at the same location.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous event-loop work after completion state dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit existing tool-invocation telemetry through the 1DS collector.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two event submissions per reported call when usage telemetry is enabled, with HTTP payload grouping and scheduling delegated to the unchanged collector; not two HTTP requests per call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same two event submissions used the same collector and telemetry gates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Collector initialization and HTTP delivery are asynchronous and not awaited by completion handling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward telemetry data to the configured trace logger, potentially backed by a log file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The same two trace-log calls per reported completion, subject to logger configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Both tool-invocation events were already passed to this appender.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing logger invocation occurs during report emission; the diff adds no log flush or file wait.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N distinct completed calls with matching starts across active chats. Duplicate completions are dropped after the timing entry is consumed. Existing result serialization scales with total result bytes; the added comparison involves only tool-name-length text.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Completion processing is synchronous on the host event loop. Reports are either emitted immediately or deferred per chat/turn until model usage or turn cleanup. Two telemetry events per distinct reported completion remain unchanged; network scheduling belongs to the existing 1DS PostChannel.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no new cache. Timing entries deduplicate completions and are deleted before reporting. Existing turn-model lookup controls immediate versus deferred emission; collector initialization uses a shared promise on cold use and reuses that promise on warm use.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced source-kind short-circuiting, duplicate suppression, caller ordering, reporter event counts, telemetry gates, and asynchronous collector transport.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Call volume and result sizes vary by workflow. No timings were measured; ordinary tool names are short, and the diff does not change full-result serialization volume.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added guarded prefix check does not establish realistically expensive repeated work, added boundary calls, or changed retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: The model requests an unavailable tool and the runtime completes it with the matching missing-tool error.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The completion is dispatched to session state first. The tracker then checks the exact name-containing prefix and computes one SHA-256 digest synchronously before storing or emitting the report. No tool execution, subprocess, filesystem lookup, or network validation is added by the classification.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Node crypto SHA-256 computation over the unavailable tool name.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One hash computation per matching unavailable-tool completion, producing a fixed 71-character sha256-prefixed identity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The original requested-name string was copied into the report without hashing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous local CPU work during completion handling, after state dispatch; no external I/O.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize the result to calculate its character count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per tracked completion, unchanged; the hash does not cause an additional serialization of the result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same result serialization preceded report construction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the two existing telemetry events with hashed identity and unknown source metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two event submissions per reported call, zero when telemetry is gated off; HTTP grouping remains collector-owned and unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same events carried the raw requested name and agentHost/failure metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No network await is introduced; delivery remains off the completion critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Trace-log the existing telemetry events through the configured logger.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same two event-log invocations; only field values change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same two events were logged with their original identity fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Unchanged logging placement with no new flush or awaited filesystem operation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: U distinct unavailable-tool completions with matching starts. Added hashing is O(sum of requested-name bytes), once per completion, not once per telemetry event and not over tool arguments or full result content.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Hashing runs synchronously on the host event loop, with no worker or request fan-out. Main and subagent completions share the same tracker behavior. Both existing telemetry events reuse the single precomputed hash.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No hash cache or additional retained collection is introduced. Repeated identical unavailable names are hashed again on distinct calls; duplicate completions for the same call are suppressed. Existing collector cold initialization remains shared and warm transport scheduling is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: hashing is guarded by agentHost source and the exact missing-tool prefix, runs once at report construction, and the resulting identity is shared by both events.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Unavailable-tool frequency and name lengths are not measured. The traced realistic input is a short tool identifier, not an unbounded tool response or document. No evidence establishes user-visible latency from this small local digest.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression. The diff introduces small linear name hashing for this subset of failures, but no realistic costly input, multiplicative fan-out, or retained-resource growth was established. The telemetry classification change is not itself a proven performance-regression fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Complete tool calls before model usage arrives, then flush reports at usage resolution or turn end/cancellation/session cleanup.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Completion preparation, including any unavailable-name hash, occurs once when the tool completes. If model usage is unresolved, the report is deferred; updateTurnModel or clearSession subsequently emits pending reports synchronously without hashing again. Turn cleanup does not wait for collector HTTP completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit pending tool reports to the existing telemetry collector.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two event submissions per pending report, 2P total at flush when enabled; HTTP requests are collector-grouped, not newly per report.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same pending reports were emitted by the same usage-resolution and cleanup loops with the same two-event count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous event preparation during flush, with asynchronous HTTP delivery not awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Trace-log pending telemetry events during report flush.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same 2P event-log invocations, subject to logger configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same pending-event loop already invoked the logging appender.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing flush-time logger calls; no new disk wait or log flush.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P pending completed-call reports per chat/turn, across all relevant main and subagent chats. Each report is flushed once; the existing queues retain one report per pending completion until usage resolution or cleanup.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing per-turn pending arrays are flushed synchronously in a loop. There is no newly introduced global concurrency burst, parallel hash work, extra emission, or changed queue policy. Collector request concurrency remains outside this diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing _turnModels map caches model resolution. _pendingToolReports entries are removed before emission on usage update or chat cleanup; timing entries, stall timers, stalled-call state, and model entries retain their pre-diff cleanup paths. The hash string replaces the report identity rather than adding another field or cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected report creation, pending-array insertion, model-resolution flush, session cleanup, subagent cleanup callers, and shared telemetry transport.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Pending report counts depend on tool activity before usage resolution. Large pre-existing flush batches may cost time, but this diff does not increase batch cardinality or change flush scheduling.
Scenarios.Verdict: No diff-introduced retention or flush regression: queue ownership, event counts, cleanup, and scheduling remain unchanged; hashing is not repeated at flush.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass for PR #349592 against base 1eb0c7511cdf93cdd228367086f0496b7f43d440. Inspected the complete four-file inventory and all diff pages, required focus-document loads, tracker lifecycle, completion callers, contributor refinement, integration coverage, and transitive telemetry serialization/logging/network paths. No actionable high-confidence performance regressions or concrete performance-regression fixes were established. Static review only; collector-internal batching limits and measured timings were not available.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
